question.text: An <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> person is parachuting and is experiencing a downward acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2.8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The mass of the parachute is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. If the upward force on the open parachute is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math>? (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9.8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></math>

solution.text:
Mass of the person M=80 kg

Mass of the parachute m=5 kg

∴ Total mass of the system =M+m=85kg

Downward acceleration a=2.8 ms-2

Let upward force =F

Applying Newton's II law of motion to this system

F=m+Mg-m+Ma

or  F=m+Mg-a

F=859.8-2.8N

=85×7 N

F=595 N=5.95×102 N

k=5.95
